citations.review_text: Bought this game because i remember sneakily watching jacksepticeye play this as a kid, a great game thats worthwhile to experience if you like the kind of humor in south park, feels more 'immersive' than fractured but whole with its ubisoft integrations flashbanging you every 20 seconds

9.5/10: A must-play for any South Park fan, dinged only by Ubisoft's bloatware

South Park: The Stick of Truth is a turn-based RPG that drops you into the show's world as the New Kid, perfectly capturing the look and humor of the series. It's extremely fun and an easy recommendation for any South Park fan, packed with easter eggs and funny moments, and it nails the show's style so well that I beat it in about three days. In my opinion it's better than The Fractured but Whole, and both are far better than Snow Day. The only thing keeping it from a perfect score is Ubisoft forcing you to download a separate app just to play a game you bought on Steam - pointless bloatware with no perceivable benefit. Overall it's a great game and one of the best South Park experiences out there.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the saving system is location-based rather than saving the exact timestamp, which can cause progress loss.

citations.review_text: Great game, a lot of fun. What I don't like is that the saving system is weird (even if you save, you will be thrown back to the last point the game made a "possibility" to save, which can cost you up to 2 minute of gameplay or even more if you did some inventory management) and that there are missable collectibles.

Game's good if you're a fan of the show — They basically took all the Game of Thrones parody episodes and made it a game! (not fully but a lot of visual aspects and soundtracks of it are here, they basically expanded the concept they were using there instead of just making it a funny spoof to get x-boxes like in the show) and I liked this game BUT it's not "perfect" and here's why:
[b]The saving in this game is terrible[/b] — they definitely improved/fixed this in the sequel (fractured but whole). Saving in this game doesn't actually save the specific moment/timestamp you save it in it's kinda location based in a way? if you really wanna continue where you left off you have to basically find a "spot" in the game that saves where you actually "are";
[b]Controller support/gameplay isn't great [/b]— This game is a lot better with keyboard/WASD and mouse than a controller, it does have Xbox controller support (and even PS controller support with steam input, you can find a good mod on Nexus Mods that replaces the Xbox buttons with PS ones and it works like a charm) but it's not the best/smoothest experience, the game is definitely "built" to be played on PC in my opinion. Other than that the game's storyline and gameplay is pretty enjoyable (the humor/vibe from the show is still in the game) and it's definitely worth the buy! 

Just don't buy the DLC costumes/Super Ultimate Pack unless you don't mind throwing money away — there's really no grand-worth it-payoff to getting them besides some small bonuses that don't really affect your gameplay in the long run and getting messages from Cartman on Facebook [spoiler]saying "The best thing about Super Samurai Spaceman DLC is the name. Seriously that's about it" if you only get the Super Samurai Spaceman Pack and "For some reason I feel as though our friendship has risen to a higher level. Perhaps even... Ultimate." if you get the Ultimate Fellowship Pack. If you buy both DLC by buying the "Super Ultimate Pack" instead Cartman…

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game does not require a third-party launcher or external account to play.

citations.review_text:
Possibly the best adaptation of a tv into a video game. It captures the feeling of an episode of South Park perfectly. It doesn't overstay it's welcome, or drag out certain scenes for too long. My biggest complaint is when doing the fart tutorials; they are kind of buggy and the timing the game gives you is off. I really recommend this game if for some reason you're a fan of the show and have not played it yet.

It also doesn't require an ubisoft account to play, so you don't have to worry about that.
♥♥♥♥ ubisoft.

This is the South Park game that does not put nonsense DRM on your PC, or require a Ubisoft nonsense login software retinal scan with a blood sample, and a foot print. It has a pretty good number of "South Park jokes," and the gameplay mechanics make sense and work well. If you enjoy the show, this game is also probably good for you. :)

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks post-game content or activities after completing the story.

citations.review_text: Great game I wish there was something to do after the story is complete.

A gem. This will be amazing for any SouthPark fan - you literally step into the cartoon. Graphics are great - story is the same bullshitting around as they always do. Would have been amazingt if they had added some choice-matters options and things to do after you have finished the main story, but I wasn't expecting it to be this good anyways. Mostly played it on PS and have finished it several times. Highly recommended.
